entities.summary: Schuyler Skaats Wheeler was an American electrical engineer and manufacturer who invented the electric fan, an electric elevator design, and the electric fire engine. He is associated with the early development of the electric motor industry, especially to do with training the blind in this industry for gainful employment. He helped develop and implement a code of ethics for electrical engineers and was associated with the electrical field in one way or another for over thirty years. Schuyler Wheeler was a scientists & inventors from Manhattan (1860-05-17, Manhattan–1923-04-20). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Schuyler Wheeler's inventions and contributions to the electric motor industry had a significant impact on the development of modern electrical engineering, particularly in training the blind for gainful employment. His code of ethics for electrical engineers also helped establish standards for the field.
